newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus sees lower H2 result.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus sees lower H2 result.

text.p: French pay-television company Canal Plus expects a lower second half profit compared to the first six months of the year, due to its investments in digital operations, finance director Laurent Perpere said on Wednesday.

"For the full year, we cannot simply multiply the (first-half) result by two, because we will have a second half loaded with charges for Canal Plus digital," he told an analysts' meeting. The charges had only been taken for two months of the first half, he added.
"We will have a net result in the second half that will be lower than the first half," he said.
Perpere confirmed a profit forecast made on Tuesday that the group expected its 1996 result to at least match last year's net attributable profit of 666 million francs.
Canal Plus yesterday reported a 1996 first-half profit of 386 million francs, up 16.6 percent.
It said its subscriber base had grown to 4,134,000 by September 15 from 4,070,000 at the end of December.
The Canalsatellite operation had 360,000 subscribers by September 15, up from 112,000 at December 31, 1995, the company said in a statement.
The new Canalsatellite digital service had received 112,000 firm orders as of September 15 and 75,000 terminals had been installed. The service will be France's first digital satellite operation.

The company expects to have 1.25 million customers in Germany by the end of this year, up from 1,064,000 in 1995, with 120,000 in Poland versus 53,000, 1.35 million in Spain versus 1,205,000, and 185,000 in Belgium, compared to 172,000.
The company's losses from non-domestic sales fell to 76 million francs in the first half from 105 million a year ago.
